text:
I'm working with pandas and keep getting a problem when merging orders with customers. I've got an order dataframe with 120,000 rows, and a customer dataframe with 9,000 rows. I want to merge customer information to each order using customer_id. But when I do a left join, I get 127,845 rows, instead of the 120,000 I would expect. Each order should only have 1 customer max. But when I merge, I get extra rows, some orders are repeated. For example, if I filter my order_id, I see rows for the same order.
I checked unique customer ids. On orders, I have 9,000 unique customer ids, same as rows. But on customers, I have 8,750 unique ids, not 9,000. So it looks like customers is the problem, and that some customers are repeated. Both dataframes have a customer_id column, and the data types look ok. Both are int64. So I'm not sure what's causing the extra duplicate rows. How do I figure out what's causing the duplicate rows, and make sure that each order is only associated with 1 customer?
